title: Quinoa & Roasted Veggie Khichdi
summary: A high-fiber, low-glycemic twist on traditional comfort khichdi using golden quinoa, yellow moong dal, and cumin-spiced squash.
ingredients: 1 cup diced zucchini and yellow squash
1 tbsp extra virgin cold-pressed olive oil
2.5 cups low-sodium vegetable broth or water
Fresh coriander and lemon wedge for serving
instructions: Heat olive oil in a deep skillet over medium heat; crackle cumin seeds until aromatic.
Add zucchini, squash, and turmeric; sauté for 3 minutes until lightly softened.
Stir in rinsed quinoa and moong dal, coating them with the spiced aromatics.
Pour in warm vegetable broth, bring to a gentle boil, then cover and simmer on low for 18 minutes.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, fluff gently, and garnish with fresh coriander and lemon juice.

title: Wild Salmon with Lemon Asparagus
summary: Omega-3 rich wild salmon fillet pan-seared with fresh crisp asparagus spears, garlic, and fresh squeezed lemon zest.
ingredients: 1 bunch thin tender asparagus, woody ends trimmed
Pinch of sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper
instructions: Pat salmon fillet completely dry with a paper towel and season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place salmon skin-side down; cook for 4-5 minutes until crisp, then flip gently for 3 minutes.
Toss asparagus and garlic directly into the pan juices around the fish for the final 3 minutes.
Drizzle with fresh lemon juice and zest right before serving warm.

title: Moong Dal & Spinach Chilla
summary: Savory high-protein breakfast crepes ground from soaked yellow lentils, blended with baby spinach, ginger, and green chilies.
ingredients: 1 cup soaked split yellow moong dal (soaked 2 hours)
1 tbsp cold-pressed sesame or olive oil
instructions: Blend the soaked moong dal, ginger, green chili, and minimal water into a smooth, pourable batter.
Fold in chopped spinach, ajwain, and rock salt.
Heat a seasoned non-stick tawa on medium; lightly grease with 1/2 tsp oil.
Pour a ladleful of batter and spread into a thin circle using the back of the spoon.
Cook for 2 minutes until golden spots appear, flip, and cook 1 more minute until crisp.

title: Avocado, Chia & Walnut Power Bowl
summary: Slow-burning monounsaturated healthy fats combined with hydrated chia seeds, crushed walnuts, and unsweetened cinnamon hemp milk.
ingredients: 2 tbsp black chia seeds, soaked in 1/2 cup unsweetened almond milk
2 tbsp raw California walnut halves, crushed
instructions: Ensure chia seeds have soaked for at least 15 minutes to form a gentle gel base.
Spoon the chia pudding base into a wide bowl.
Top artfully with fresh avocado cubes, crushed raw walnuts, and pumpkin seeds.
Dust lightly with Ceylon cinnamon for enhanced natural insulin sensitivity and enjoy immediately.

title: Mediterranean Herb Lentil & Kale Stew
summary: Rich in soluble fiber that slows carbohydrate absorption, simmered with brown lentils, Tuscan kale, oregano, and crushed tomatoes.
ingredients: 3/4 cup brown or green pardina lentils
2 cups chopped curly or lacinato kale
3 cups water or light vegetable stock
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil in a soup pot until translucent.
Add lentils, tomatoes, rosemary, and water; bring to a rolling simmer.
Cover and simmer for 22 minutes until lentils are tender yet hold their shape.
Stir in kale ribbons during the last 5 minutes of cooking until deep green and wilted.
Season with cracked black pepper and a drop of apple cider vinegar.

title: Spiced Roasted Chickpeas & Almonds
summary: Crunchy oven-roasted kabuli chickpeas paired with whole almonds, dusted with smoked paprika, roasted cumin, and black salt.
ingredients: 1 can (400g) organic chickpeas, rinsed and thoroughly dried
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Thoroughly dry chickpeas between towels; removing moisture ensures optimal crunch.
Toss chickpeas and almonds with avocado oil and spices in a mixing bowl.
Spread evenly in a single layer and roast for 20-25 minutes, shaking the tray halfway.
Allow to cool completely to reach peak crispness before storing in an airtight jar.
